The bridge E-F carries the most, 22 in accent, then C-E 18, and D-E and F-G 13; the triangle edges A-B and C-D carry the least, 8." width="100%"} Load (Goh, Kahng and Kim, 2001) models traffic that is routed hop by hop: every node sends one unit to every node it can reach, and at each step the traffic is split equally among the neighbors that are one hop closer to the destination. An edge's load is the total traffic that crosses it. It is the edge counterpart of `load_centrality()` and, like it, can differ from `edge_betweenness_centrality()`, which splits traffic in proportion to the number of shortest paths instead of equally at each step. Edges are unweighted and path lengths count hops. Parallel edges are treated as one link and each carries the full load. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [cutoff]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Only follow paths of at most this many hops. If `None` (default), all paths count. [attr_name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Name of the edge attribute to store loads in. If `None` (default), uses `"edge_load_centrality"`. [return_dict]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, returns a dictionary instead of self. If `False` (default), stores the loads as an edge attribute and returns self for chaining. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Union[dict[int, float], Graph]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `return_dict=` is `True`: a dictionary mapping edge IDs to loads. If `return_dict=` is `False` (default): returns self. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `cutoff=` is less than 1. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} One breadth-first search per node, with the load pushed back from the farthest nodes towards the source, $O(V E)$. As in NetworkX's `edge_load_centrality()`, every edge starts each search with one unit, so values are not normalized. NetworkX keys the result by node pairs in both orientations, which always carry the same value; EdgeCase keys it by edge ID. ## Examples {.doc-examples} In a diamond `A-B-D`, `A-C-D` with a tail `D-E`, the load from the tail splits equally over the two sides of the diamond: ::: {#ce035dc8 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D", "E"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("A", "C"), ("B", "D"), ("C", "D"), ("D", "E")]) ) loads = graph.edge_load_centrality(return_dict=True) label = graph.get_label_from_id {"-".join(label(n) for n in graph.get_node_ids_by_edge_id(e)): x for e, x in loads.items()} ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` {'A-B': 7.5, 'A-C': 7.5, 'B-D': 9.5, 'C-D': 9.5, 'D-E': 9.0} ``` ::: :::
